first_impression.reaction: James's dad's side is Samoan-Australian and his aunties already have opinions, so I Googled it. The intro is calm and clear: 'the meeting of two families' is exactly what we're hearing at home, and it promised the day in order plus what Australians need to know. The 'You Did Not Know?' headline is clickbait, but the writing underneath is better than that.

journey.quote: A Samoan wedding is not only the joining of two people. It is the meeting of two families, carried out in the way of fa'a Samoa: chiefs and orators speak, fine mats change hands, the church blesses the marriage and the whole family sits down to eat.
journey.reaction: Good. Not gushy, and it tells me the shape of the day in one sentence. Kept going.

journey.quote: A Samoan wedding is led by the aiga, the extended family, and its matai, so the families' wishes shape the day as much as the couple's.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, said up front. That's the conversation we need to have before we pick anything.

journey.section: 1. Fa'a Samoa, matai and the families behind the wedding
journey.quote: Te Ara, the New Zealand government encyclopedia, calls aiga the bedrock of fa'asamoa.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but it's 'the tourism authority describes', 'Te Papa describes', 'Te Ara notes' over and over. Sections 1 and 2 read like a museum essay. I started skimming for the bits that tell me what to do.

journey.section: 2. The families meet: orators and formal speeches
journey.quote: Ask early who will speak for each family, and build the run sheet around the speeches and presentations rather than squeezing them in.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. I'd have assumed speeches go after dinner for ten minutes. Clearly not.

journey.section: 3. Fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families
journey.quote: Give the presentation unhurried time and a sheltered, dignified space, and agree handling, display and transport with the family, not with suppliers.
journey.reaction: Insider-level advice. Heirloom mats on a plane or in a venue storeroom is exactly the kind of thing I wouldn't think of until it went wrong.

journey.quote: For a real celebration from our pages, see [Mercy and Chanel's traditional Samoan wedding](/a-traditional-samoan-wedding-celebration).
journey.reaction: A real wedding. I'd click this before anything else, though it doesn't say where or when it was, or whether you planned it.

journey.section: 8. The wedding feast and the umu
journey.quote: For a destination wedding, ask early whether your venue allows an umu on the grounds, or whether the family will cook off site and bring the food in.
journey.reaction: Great question I'd never have asked. But again, it's me asking. Is that something you'd sort with the venue?

journey.section: 9. What UNESCO says about the 'ie Samoa
journey.quote: UNESCO describes the 'Ie Samoa as a finely hand-woven pandanus mat with two rows of green and red feathers at the hem, which can take up to several months and even years to make.
journey.reaction: We already covered the mats and the months-or-years weaving in section 3. This felt like a repeat. Skimmed it.

journey.section: 10. Weddings in Samoa: Travel and etiquette
journey.quote: Sunday activities are extremely limited and alcohol can't be sold, though hotels and resorts operate normally; be respectful passing through villages.
journey.reaction: Very practical. If the wedding is on a Saturday and guests stay Sunday, that changes the plan. Same with 'Check every guest's passport expiry when invitations go out.'

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller advice for Samoa](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/pacific/samoa) is "Exercise normal safety precautions", updated 5 August 2026, with an ongoing dengue outbreak since 2025.
journey.reaction: I'd rather know, but my parents will fixate on 'dengue' and 'cyclone season'. And there's nothing about where 80 guests would stay, what the venues are like or how Nana gets from the airport to Savai'i. 'Couples who marry in Samoa tend to choose Upolu or Savai'i' is one line.

journey.quote: Before you book, put these questions to Samoa's Births, Deaths and Marriages registry and the Australian High Commission in Apia:
journey.reaction: The question list is genuinely helpful. But it reads as 'you go and ask them'. The legal side is the thing I want someone else to sort.

journey.quote: The same questions apply: who speaks for each family, where the mats will be presented, and whether the reception venue can host an umu or a full family catering crew.
journey.reaction: Realistically this is us: a Sydney wedding with the Samoan side fully involved. It's only a short paragraph, though. I'd want timings and how a planner works alongside a big family crew.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and guest rooms, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee and inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: This answers two of my biggest worries: who's accountable, and currency surprises. Best line on the page for me.

unanswered_questions: Did you plan Mercy and Chanel's wedding? Where and when was it? Have you run other Samoan or Samoan-Australian weddings?
How does a Wedded Advisor work alongside a big family that is cooking, speaking and organising its own parts of the day? Who runs the run sheet?
Would you handle the umu question, mat transport and cultural space with the venue, or is that on our family?
If we married in Samoa, where would 60 to 90 guests stay, and how would older relatives get from the airport to Upolu or Savai'i?
Will you help gather and chase the Samoan marriage paperwork and the CNI, or only point us to the registry?
What happens with guests and the plan if a cyclone hits in the November to April season?

turn_offs_found.quote: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
turn_offs_found.why: Clickbait headline. The article is more thoughtful than its title.

turn_offs_found.quote: Te Papa describes 'ie toga as a valuable presented in ceremonies that cement relationships between people, and worn as a garment on important occasions by high-ranking matai and taupou, the daughters of chiefs.
turn_offs_found.why: One of many 'X describes' attributions. Repeated this much it reads like a footnoted essay, not an expert who has been to these weddings.

would_share_with: James's dad and aunties (the speeches, mats and taualuga sections)
My parents (only 'Bringing Samoan traditions home', not the dengue and cyclone part)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through dates, islands or a wedding at home, a Wedded Advisor is happy to start the conversation.
cta_reaction.why: No hard sell, and the written fee in AUD is a real plus. But I'd click the Mercy and Chanel real wedding first and look for proof you've worked with a Samoan family before. If that checks out, I'd enquire.

top_3_changes: Trim the repeated 'Te Papa describes', 'the tourism authority describes' attributions so it reads like an expert guide, and fold the UNESCO section into the fine mats section rather than repeating it.

Expand 'Bringing Samoan traditions home' with real run-of-day logistics (how long speeches and mat presentations take, umu and family catering at a venue, where the planner fits alongside the family).

Add a line on what a Samoa wedding looks like for guests (staying, getting there, cyclone-season back-up) and say plainly what the Wedded Advisor does on paperwork, and give the real wedding link a venue, date and whether you planned it.
